Primary proposition.statement="For the real mean-zero normalized 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, use the source twisted coefficients y_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t) hat U(k,t), k!=0, with ||y||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|y_k|^2. for s>=0, finite T_s>0, initial dot H^s datum y0 and an upper bound B0 for its L2 norm, the source Galerkin flows have sup_[0,T_s] dot H^s norm bounded by a constant depending only on s,T_s,||y0||_(dot H^s),B0, uniformly in Galerkin dimension. For s>0 a subsequence converges to a distributional limiting solution with the same bound (the limiting statement uses strong L^p_t H^sigma convergence for 0<sigma<s and 1<p<infinity and weak-star L^infinity_t dot H^s convergence). The uniqueness and continuity claims for s>1/2 and for 0<s<=1/2 make this solution unique, C([0,T_s];dot H^s), L2 conserving and Lipschitz continuous in the initial dot H^s data. At s=0, for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T_s];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation and Lipschitz continuous in the initial data. For the two-flow estimate, for theta in (-1,0], if ||y0||_2+||z0||_2<=B, then their two source twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,T_s]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B,theta)*C_B(theta)^(T_s)*||y0-z0||_(dot H^theta). All these claims concern the source equation and its twist, not the target sign convention."; duplicate source.statement="For the real mean-zero normalized 2*pi-periodic source equation U_t=U U_x+U_xxx, use the source twisted coefficients y_k(t)=exp(i*k^3*t) hat U(k,t), k!=0, with ||y||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|y_k|^2. Theorems 4.2–4.3: for s>=0, finite T_s>0, initial dot H^s datum y0 and an upper bound B0 for its L2 norm, the source Galerkin flows have sup_[0,T_s] dot H^s norm bounded by a constant depending only on s,T_s,||y0||_(dot H^s),B0, uniformly in Galerkin dimension. For s>0 a subsequence converges to a distributional limiting solution with the same bound (Theorem 4.3 uses strong L^p_t H^sigma convergence for 0<sigma<s and 1<p<infinity and weak-star L^infinity_t dot H^s convergence). Theorem 5.1 for s>1/2 and Theorem 6.3 for 0<s<=1/2 make this solution unique, C([0,T_s];dot H^s), L2 conserving and Lipschitz continuous in the initial dot H^s data. Theorem 6.4: for s=0 there is a unique C([0,T_s];dot H^0) solution obtained by smooth approximation and Lipschitz continuous in the initial data. Theorem 6.5: for theta in (-1,0], if ||y0||_2+||z0||_2<=B, then their two source twisted flows satisfy sup_[0,T_s]||y-z||_(dot H^theta)<=C'(B,theta)*C_B(theta)^(T_s)*||y0-z0||_(dot H^theta). All these claims concern the source equation and its twist, not the target sign convention.". They must match exactly.
